suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-16 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited National Comorbidity Survey Replication Adolescent Supplement found bulimia nervosa significantly comorbid with mood disorders and many other DSM-IV disorders in a nationally representative adolescent sample. Require independently established bulimia nervosa and separately established depressive disorder; the cited nationally representative adolescent survey reported substantial bulimia nervosa comorbidity with mood disorders without establishing onset order or direction, and its adolescent sample should not be overgeneralized to adult populations. Preserve obesity and metabolic disease, other eating pathology, substance use, medications, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from eating-disorder symptoms, weight concern, or role impairment alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that bulimia nervosa caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the bounded association the located eating-disorder dental literature supports: a 2023 PRISMA systematic review and meta-analysis of 31 studies reports erosive tooth wear in 54.4 percent of patients with bulimia nervosa against 26.7 percent with anorexia nervosa and 42.1 percent of all 1,699 eating-disorder patients, with bulimia nervosa carrying more than ten times the odds of dental erosion of healthy individuals (OR 10.383, 95 percent CI 4.882-22.086) and self-induced vomiting carrying more than sixteen times the odds (OR 16.176, 95 percent CI 1.438-181.918) (PMID 37834805); the 2015 systematic review and meta-analysis of ten controlled studies (556 eating-disorder patients and 556 controls) reports approximately five times the odds of dental erosion in eating-disorder patients (95 percent CI 3.31-7.58), rising to OR 7.32 in those practicing self-induced vomiting, with higher DMFS scores (mean difference 3.07, 95 percent CI 0.66-5.48) and reduced salivary flow (OR 2.24, 95 percent CI 1.44-3.51) (PMID 26429686); and a 2024 systematic review of 32 studies confirms the association with erosion while reporting gingival recession, dentinal hypersensitivity and salivary-flow thresholds as receiving increasing rather than settled support (PMID 38915100). The registered claim is the narrowest these anchors jointly permit: that bulimia nervosa in its self-induced-vomiting presentation is associated with prevalent erosive tooth wear consistent with chronic gastric-acid exposure, with the vomiting-stratified odds ratios supplying the exposure gradient, and with NO anchor measuring incidence, onset order or reversibility.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of erosive tooth wear is established for any individual by these anchors: all three are cross-sectional prevalence designs, so their odds ratios are PREVALENCE odds and establish neither that the erosion postdates the eating disorder nor that it would not have occurred without it; the vomiting-stratified OR 16.176 rests on an extremely wide confidence interval (1.438-181.918) indicating sparse exposed data, and the pooled bulimia-versus-healthy OR of 10.383 spans 4.882-22.086 across a small study base; eating-disorder samples are selected toward treatment-seeking and disclosure-ready patients, so under-ascertainment of both the vomiting behavior and its duration is expected and none of the denominators is a population denominator; erosive tooth wear is multifactorial in etiology, and no anchor can separate gastric-acid exposure from dietary acid, xerostomia or abrasive hygiene within an individual. Individual claims require independently established bulimia nervosa with a dated record of self-induced vomiting frequency and duration, a dental examination documenting an erosion pattern consistent with perimolysis (palatal and lingual enamel surfaces of the maxillary teeth), and exclusion of extrinsic dietary acid (citrus, soft drinks, acidic sports drinks, wine), gastroesophageal reflux and rumination, occupational acid exposure, medication-induced xerostomia and mechanical abrasion from abrasive dentifrices or hard brushing before any attribution.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized acid-dissolution pathway (perimolysis): repetitive exposure of enamel to gastric hydrochloric acid during self-induced vomiting drops oral pH below the enamel demineralization threshold and chemically dissolves hydroxyapatite at the palatal and lingual surfaces, the pathway the vomiting-stratified odds ratios (OR 7.32 and OR 16.176) track directly; reduced salivary flow (OR 2.24 in the controlled meta-analysis) removes buffering and clearance that would otherwise limit the exposure, and acidic dietary habits add a second acid source, so MULTIFACTORIAL is the closest available mechanism category although the dominant vector is chemical (acid) rather than mechanical, metabolic or nutritional: the schema's strict category list carries NO chemical-injury category, and that vocabulary-imperfect fit is disclosed on the edge rather than concealed (the batch-83 vocabulary-mismatch precedent). Whether any individual's erosion was produced by gastric acid rather than by dietary acid, xerostomia or abrasion remains hypothesized until the erosion pattern is read against the documented behavioral history.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review-and-meta-analysis prevalence class and deliberately no stronger: this is the FIRST dental route from this identity and the FIRST registered incoming edge to dental-abrasion-erosion-abfraction, whose only registered relationship is its own outgoing dentin-hypersensitivity edge. THE MECHANISM DISTINCTION AGAINST THE BATCH-81 REFUSAL IS STATED EXPLICITLY because it changes what the edge may claim: batch 81 WITHHELD rumination-syndrome to dental-abrasion-erosion-abfraction as MECHANISM-UNSUPPORTED on the reasoning that rumination regurgitates undigested food without the gastric-acid exposure that drives erosive tooth wear in bulimia nervosa, and the bulimia route is registered precisely because its anchors MEASURE the acid-exposure presentation, the self-induced-vomiting strata carrying OR 7.32 and OR 16.176 against weaker gradients without documented vomiting, so the edge's evidence is the vomiting pathway and may not be extended to purging behaviors without documented acid exposure, to eating disorders at large, or to the withheld rumination route; the anorexia nervosa figure (26.7 percent) is comorbidity context in the same anchor and is not a claim window. A TARGET-SCOPE DISCLOSURE is carried on the face of the edge: the catalog identity is the umbrella Dental Abrasion / Erosion / Abfraction while EVERY located anchor measures EROSION (perimolysis) only, so the evidence supports the erosion member of the umbrella and neither the abrasive-wear nor the abfraction members, following the slap-tear and rotator-cuff target-scope precedent; the identity's registered outgoing edge to dentin-hypersensitivity is untouched and no chain from this edge through it is claimed.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: All three anchors are cross-sectional prevalence designs, so NO located anchor measures erosion incidence in bulimia nervosa, establishes that erosion follows the eating disorder in time, or reports reversibility with sustained remission and vomiting cessation; the vomiting-stratified OR 16.176 has an extremely wide confidence interval (1.438-181.918) and the bulimia-versus-healthy OR 10.383 spans 4.882-22.086 across a small study base; eating-disorder ascertainment is treatment-selected and disclosure-dependent, so both vomiting prevalence and duration are under-measured; the umbrella target's abrasion and abfraction members have NO supporting evidence on this edge; and the 2024 review reports that non-erosion oro-dental outcomes in this population are supported by emerging rather than settled evidence.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Extrinsic dietary acid (citrus, soft drinks, acidic sports drinks, wine, vinegar diets) producing erosion independent of any eating disorder
Gastroesophageal reflux disease and rumination syndrome as non-vomiting sources of gastric acid reaching the enamel
Medication-induced xerostomia and reduced salivary buffering (antidepressants, antihistamines, stimulants) worsening erosive wear
Mechanical abrasion from abrasive dentifrices, hard brushing or occupational grinding, and abfraction from occlusal loading, which the umbrella target also covers but no anchor measures
Dental caries, attrition and age-related wear misread as erosive lesions in the absence of a documented erosion pattern
